brief.headline: KOSPI whipsaws 4%+ intraday; Hynix sold, Samsung bought as HBM margins compress and CoWoS gap narrows
brief.summary: <cite index="40-4,40-5">KOSPI plunged over 4% at open before recovering to close -0.54% as Samsung and SK Hynix reversed deep deficits to trade positive</cite>, with <cite index="41-1,41-25,41-26,41-27">top 1% traders at Mirae Asset net-buying Samsung at ₩246,750 while net-selling SK Hynix at ₩1,784,000</cite>. Memory cycle enters late-stage pricing deceleration: <cite index="10-1,16-6">TrendForce projects Q3 DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ and NAND +10-15% QoQ</cite>, down from <cite index="14-10">Q1's extraordinary 93-98% QoQ surge</cite>. <cite index="4-2,4-15">HBM3E remains dominant through 2026 with pricing power intact; SK Hynix is sole supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-gen HBM4 at scale</cite>, while <cite index="30-5,30-7">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120k-140k wafers</cite>. <cite index="19-3,19-7">Hyperscaler capex guidance totals ~$725B for 2026, up 77% YoY</cite>, but <cite index="9-7">SK Hynix expects only minimal-to-modest HBM3E price downtick in 2026 while HBM4 commands 40% premium even after 50% cost-per-bit increase</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Short-term divergence favors Samsung as value play vs. Hynix profit-taking. <cite index="41-17,41-19,41-25,41-27">Smart money rotated into Samsung (trading ₩246,750, -3.2%) on weakness while exiting SK Hynix (₩1,784,000, -3.15%) amid profit-taking</cite> after <cite index="39-13">both names fell 9-14% intraday July 2</cite>. Relative call: Samsung near-term catch-up supported by <cite index="44-8">Q3 2025 HBM share recovery to 35% vs. Hynix 53%</cite> and customer commentary that "Samsung is back" on HBM4 qualification, while <cite index="9-8">Hynix's HBM4 first-mover premium (40% ASP lift) faces 50% cost headwind</cite>. However, <cite index="5-3">Hynix controls 57% global HBM revenue (Q4 2025) vs. Samsung 22%</cite>, preserving structural edge. Mid-cycle positioning: underweight both on margin compression risk as <cite index="16-18,16-19">TrendForce flags declining buyer willingness-to-pay rather than supply relief—prices already so high PC/smartphone OEMs cannot accept every further increase</cite>. Watch <cite index="43-9,43-10">new 30M won minimum for single-stock leveraged ETFs</cite> capping retail inflows.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="14-10,14-14,14-15">Q1 2026 DRAM contracts rose 93-98% QoQ (buyers paid double vs. Q4 2025); Q2 deceleration began, and for first time this cycle NAND rising faster than DRAM</cite>. <cite index="10-1,16-6">Q3 forecast: DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ—still double-digit but sequential moderation</cite>. <cite index="4-17">BofA forecasts 2026 DRAM revenue +51% YoY, NAND +45%, with ASPs +30%+</cite>. Supply discipline holding: <cite index="18-5,18-6">Samsung and SK Hynix (70% global DRAM) signaled no aggressive capacity expansion; suppliers prioritizing profitability over volume</cite>. Demand bifurcation: <cite index="14-19">AI-driven pull on server DRAM and enterprise SSDs hasn't flinched, but consumer destruction is genuine—global smartphone shipments expected to fall 14% in 2026</cite>. <cite index="14-25,14-26">First genuine strain signal: buyers no longer chasing higher spot quotes and NAND spot trading gone quiet, even as headline numbers stay green</cite>. HBM crowding-out continues: <cite index="18-25">Micron noted 3-to-1 conversion ratio between HBM and DDR5 wafer capacity, meaning every HBM ramp directly compresses general-purpose memory supply</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-3,4-19">Top three memory makers have already allocated full HBM output for 2026; Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="4-2,4-27">HBM3E remains dominant AI memory through 2026 with pricing power intact until new capacity comes online after 2027</cite>. <cite index="9-3">UBS channel checks indicate SK Hynix will secure largely stable ~50% market share in 2026 HBM bit shipments</cite>, while <cite index="9-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb</cite>. <cite index="9-7,9-8">Hynix expects minimal-to-modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs. 2025 as more suppliers come online; far more important is HBM4 first-mover premium of ~40% higher prices vs. outgoing generation, even after absorbing 50% rise in cost-per-bit</cite>. <cite index="4-15">SK Hynix is only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-gen HBM4 at scale</cite>; <cite index="4-26">UBS forecasts Hynix could take ~70% of HBM4 market for Nvidia's Rubin platform in 2026</cite>. Samsung recovery: <cite index="44-8">customers stating 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, though Hynix held 53% HBM share in Q3 2025 vs. Samsung 35%</cite>. Structural tightness persists: <cite index="4-11">HBM3E consumes roughly 3x the wafer area of standard DDR5 due to larger dies and yield losses from vertical stacking</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: KOSPI V-shaped recovery: Samsung/SK Hynix reverse 4%+ opening losses to close positive
news_pulse.implication: Panic selling subsided intraday; smart money rotated into Samsung while taking profits on SK Hynix per Mirae top-1% flow. Volatility signals late-cycle positioning uncertainty.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS monthly capacity reaching 120k-140k wafers in 2026 eases HBM packaging bottleneck. Reduces allocation premium for Nvidia/hyperscalers; watch margin compression as lead-times normalize.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 2026 memory pricing decelerates: DRAM +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Sequential deceleration from Q1's 93-98% QoQ surge. Driver: buyer resistance, not supply relief. Consumer demand destruction (smartphones -14% YoY) offsetting AI server pull.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex hits $725B (+77% YoY); Goldman sees $1.1T in 2027
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Microsoft $190B, Google $175-185B, Meta $115-135B sustains HBM/server DRAM demand through 2027. Monetization risk rising—Meta shares fell 9.25% May 1 on capex increase.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix sole HBM4 volume supplier; UBS sees 50% 2026 share, 40% price premium
news_pulse.implication: HBM4 first-mover advantage intact despite 50% cost-per-bit increase. Hynix likely secures 70% of Nvidia Rubin platform. Samsung HBM4 qualification progress ('Samsung is back') narrows gap.

news_pulse.headline: Top 1% traders buy Samsung, sell SK Hynix in 4%+ KOSPI plunge
news_pulse.implication: Smart money divergence: Samsung bargain-hunt at ₩246,750 vs. Hynix profit-taking at ₩1,784,000. Suggests near-term relative outperformance for Samsung on valuation/HBM4 catch-up.

news_pulse.headline: South Korea unveils 30M won minimum for leveraged single-stock ETFs
news_pulse.implication: Retail capitulation signal. Leveraged Samsung/SK Hynix ETFs amplified losses; new 30M won minimum (vs. 3M prior) curtails speculative inflows. Removes marginal bid.

news_pulse.headline: Memory demand/supply bifurcation: AI enterprise strong, consumer destruction real
news_pulse.implication: Server DRAM/enterprise SSD pull from AI hasn't flinched, but global smartphone shipments -14% YoY in 2026. PC OEMs built high client SSD inventory H1 2026, declining willingness to accept further hikes.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated implied vol post-selloff; single-stock leveraged ETF unwind ongoing. <cite index="43-9,43-10">New 30M won cash minimum for leveraged ETFs (up from 3M effective minimum) curtails retail re-entry</cite>. <cite index="43-11,43-12">KB Financial flags leveraged ETFs increasingly resemble speculative vehicles; prolonged slump risk if volatility persists</cite>. No clear capitulation in options skew yet—watch for put-selling resumption as signal of institutional re-entry. <cite index="39-3">SK Hynix ADR listing on Nasdaq July 10</cite> may provide US options liquidity and arbitrage opportunities vs. KRX.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung/SK Hynix price action into US open—July 10 SK Hynix Nasdaq ADR debut could drive arb flows
Any HBM4 customer allocation updates from hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Google earnings season approaching)
TSMC CoWoS utilization/lead-time commentary—narrowing gap to 10% by year-end changes packaging bottleneck thesis
Spot DRAM/NAND pricing updates from TrendForce or DRAMeXchange—watch for first negative prints signaling peak
Retail leveraged ETF redemption flow under new 30M won minimum—magnitude determines technical overhang duration
